result:
The morning light filters through the leaves like spilled honey, and for a moment the entire forest seems to hold its breath. I’ve always loved how nature doesn’t perform for us; it simply exists with a kind of effortless dignity that humans spend lifetimes trying to imitate.

Lately I’ve been thinking about memory and how it behaves like a mischievous editor. It cuts scenes, rearranges timelines, adds dramatic lighting to ordinary moments. The summer I turned eleven smells like cut grass and stolen peaches even though I’m certain we never had a peach tree. Yet the memory insists. It has decided that’s the scent of childhood and refuses to negotiate.

There’s something beautiful about this unreliability. If our memories were perfect recordings, we’d be trapped inside them. Instead they become stories we tell ourselves, evolving with us. The boy who was terrified of the dark becomes the man who smiles at that same fear, recognizing it as the price of having an imagination large enough to populate shadows with monsters.

I’ve started collecting small wonders the way other people collect coins or stamps. Today it was the way steam rose from my coffee in perfect Fibonacci spirals. Yesterday it was watching a crow solve a three-stage puzzle for a peanut. Tomorrow it will be something else, equally ordinary, equally miraculous.

The world is so achingly temporary and yet so stubbornly persistent. Every moment is a small rebellion against entropy. I find that thought comforting. We are all, in our own ridiculous ways, refusing to disappear quietly.

(Word count: 248)
